title: CluesRequest
description:
A request for People enrichment's Clues: the people a load of the version could look up.
It reads the tables and runs the create passes that make the people the `[enrichments]`
item enriches, as the load would, with no graph: every mapping with a create binding of the
item's type, and the mappings they look up. A row too large for a write
(`max_request_bytes`, with the load's id) is left out as the load leaves it out.

load.description:
The load the people would be looked up for, which Ingest will create: a row's size
counts its id, as the load's chunks do.

max_request_bytes.description:
The largest request body the load's Helix proxy takes, as Ingest's
`helix.max_request_bytes`: a row whose write wouldn't fit is left out.

request_id.description: The idempotency key: a retry sends the same one.

sources.description:
The tables, as the load's Ingest will be sent them; file paths are under the files
root. Sources routed to extraction are left out.

DocumentFile.description: One staged document of a document set ([`SourceAccess::Documents`](crate::SourceAccess::Documents)).

path.description: The staged text, under the files root.

title.description: The document's title, as the backend shows it.

delimiter.description: The field delimiter, one ASCII character.

header.description: Whether the first row names the fields.

LoadId.description: One load of an approved version into a graph: the id of the backend job that creates it, such as a ULID. One or more printable ASCII characters, no space.

MediaType.description:
Document formats that take the LLM path. Tables and code take deterministic routes and are
not documents.

oneOf.description: Markdown: sections break at headings too.

Observed.description:
When a source's data was observed, as the caller pinned the source: the connector's sync
its snapshot was taken at, or the upload of its file. The transactions of the source's rows
record it ([`Origin::Rows`]), so a load tells when what its rows say held at the source.

oneOf.description: A connector's sync of the source's table.

at.description: When the sync observed the table.

change_seq.description: The table's change sequence number the snapshot holds every change up to.

sync_id.description: The sync, by the backend's id.

oneOf.description: The upload of the source's file.

document_id.description: The uploaded document, by the backend's id.

Route.description: How a source's data enters the graph.

oneOf.description: Through mappings; its facts carry this confidence.

trust.description: How far to trust what its rows state; 1 unless the user says otherwise.

SourceAccess.description:
How to read a source. A presigned URL for a file is not taken yet: the readers read local
paths.

oneOf.description: A Postgres database, through a short-lived read-only role.

dsn_env.description: The environment variable that holds the connection string.

path.description: Where it is; a relative path is taken from the base directory the caller gives.

oneOf.description:
A document set: some of its documents, staged as local text files. Extraction reads the
set's documents through `mappings.toml`'s `[extractions]` routes, not through the table
readers.

A table's changes since a load's position, in place of its whole snapshot: taken only by
an Ingest with `reload: "diff"`. A JSON Lines file of one change per key, in any order:
`{"op": "upsert", "key": {..}, "row": {..}}`, the row as a snapshot holds it, or `{"op":
"delete", "key": {..}}`, where `key` holds the table's primary-key columns. The source's
`fingerprint` is that of the snapshot the changes lead to, and its `observed` sync's
`change_seq` is `to_seq`.

from_seq.description:
The change sequence the load's position in the table must hold: the file holds every
change after it.

path.description: Where the file is; a relative path is taken from the base directory the caller gives.

to_seq.description: The change sequence the file holds every change up to.

SourceDescriptor.description: A source the turn may read; see [`TurnRequest`] for one in JSON.

description.description: What it holds, in the user's words.

display_name.description: What the user calls it; kept out of the artifacts by the leak guard.

fingerprint.description:
What identifies its data: a file's content hash, or the backend's snapshot id of a
database. Seeds and the tools' memo depend on it, so changed data is measured afresh.

id.description: The opaque id artifacts name it by.

observed.description:
When its data was observed, if the backend knows: the connector sync its snapshot was
taken at, or the upload of its file. An Ingest records it on the transaction of each
chunk of the source's rows; a turn reads nothing of it.

route.description: How its data enters the graph, as the backend decides.
